fallback.text: A neighbour asks for help on day 0: you ought to go within two days. You do not go, so on day 2 that duty is violated. A second, contrary-to-duty norm now applies: if you did not help, you ought at least to call within a day. The call on day 4 meets that deadline, so the repair duty is fulfilled while the first duty stays violated. A third norm forbids noise at night and is kept. The picture shows one row per norm along the days: a red mark where a norm was violated, a green mark where it was fulfilled, an amber mark where it is still in force. This is Chisholm's contrary-to-duty paradox (1963) told in time, the way norms with deadlines are checked in multi-agent systems.
